clue.text: Newlyweds purchase a little ring in a Yorkshire town

indicators.note: newly suggests the following letters are made anew, signalling a rearrangement of weds
the small piece of ring goes inside the word for purchase

parts.note: to purchase is to buy

indicators.note: only a little of the word ring is used, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A just-married couple go shopping for a modest ring in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newlyweds' hides its own signal: 'Newly' rearranges WEDS into DEWS. Then 'a little' gives R from ring, put 'in' BUY to make BURY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewsbury is a market town in West Yorkshire, England.

clue.text: Lives initially documented by science-fiction writer

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of documented

parts.note: H G Wells wrote The War of the Worlds and The Time Machine

explanation.surface: Biographies were first recorded by a sci-fi author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' poses as a plural noun, biographies, but is the verb: resides.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside, so dwells means lives somewhere.

clue.text: All sacred in recital?

indicators.note: a recital is spoken out, so the word for sacred is heard rather than seen

parts.note: sacred means holy

explanation.surface: Everything is holy when performed in a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholly means entirely, in all respects.

clue.text: Disheartened rabbit — one subdued by monster

indicators.note: losing its heart, the word for rabbit drops its middle letter

parts.note: a bunny is a rabbit
the Roman numeral for one is I
P, for piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: A dejected rabbit, a lone animal cowed by a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes the central N of BUNNY to leave BUNY.
explanation.definitionFit: The bunyip is a creature of Australian Aboriginal legend said to lurk in swamps.

clue.text: Is it eloquent or arch, perhaps? Don't answer that!

definitions.text: Is it eloquent or arch, perhaps? Don't answer that!

parts.words: Is it eloquent or arch, perhaps? Don't answer that!
parts.note: the opening asks whether a speech is grand, then the order not to reply describes a query posed purely for effect

explanation.definitionFit: A query asked only for effect, with no reply expected, is the figure of speech meant.

clue.text: A writer mostly associated with a group of stars

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a quill is an old pen, something that writes

explanation.surface: A pen-wielding author is linked with a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquila, the Eagle, is a named constellation, a group of stars in the sky.

clue.text: See 4
They provide cover in certain empty rooms

parts.note: certain means sure

indicators.note: emptied of its inside, rooms keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Bare rooms are where the cover comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves R and S from rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurers are companies that offer insurance cover against loss.

clue.text: A nymph like this may be seen in the neighbourhood

indicators.note: the word for like this goes inside the word for neighbourhood

parts.note: the neighbourhood is the local area
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: Someone like this sprite might be spotted locally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the neighbourhood' looks like part of the surface's setting, but it supplies letters; 'A nymph' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arethusa is a nymph of Greek myth who was turned into a spring.

clue.text: Cat — without tail, so it's said

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a tail is an end
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat has lost its tail, or so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', inviting a cat with a letter removed; here it is the old sense, outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to pronounce or state, so enounced means uttered or declared.

clue.text: Monster is seen writhing

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the letters of is seen are contorted

explanation.surface: A monster is spotted wriggling about.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the nickname of the Loch Ness Monster of Scottish legend.

clue.text: They stop the traffic when noted ship has sailed off

parts.note: the song On the Good Ship Lollipop, sung by Shirley Temple, names a famous ship of music

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are disordered, gone wrong

explanation.surface: Traffic halts at the departure of a famous vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' means famous through music: the Shirley Temple song. Lollipop ladies are British school crossing wardens holding a round stop sign on a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing patrol staff in Britain halt cars so children can cross the road, wielding round lollipop-shaped signs.

clue.text: Formality observed when celeb goes to church

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: Etiquette is noticed when a famous person attends a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch means stiffness or rigid formality of manner, as in a starchy person.

clue.text: Old farm worker with bald head stands out in jail

indicators.note: out means the word for stands goes outside

parts.note: to stand something is to bear it, so stands gives bears
a hind is an archaic word for a farm labourer

indicators.note: the head of bald is its first letter

explanation.surface: A balding old farmhand is conspicuous behind the prison walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands out' reads as 'is conspicuous', but 'out' is the container signal, with 'head' taking the first letter of bald.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind bars is an idiom meaning imprisoned.

clue.text: Furniture with whiskers

definitions.meaning: a sideboard is a dining-room cabinet for crockery
the British word for side whiskers, known elsewhere as sideburns

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both cupboards for dining rooms and hair grown down the cheeks.

clue.text: Phantom post office disappearing when parcel post is deregulated?

indicators.note: the letters for post office vanish from the mix
freed of rules, the remaining letters of parcel post are reordered

explanation.surface: A ghostly post office vanishes once the parcel service is privatised.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PO out of PARCELPOST to leave PARCELST, which 'deregulated' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectral means ghostly, like a phantom; here it is adjectival, as in phantom limb.

clue.text: A member of the family, who's left out, showed off

indicators.note: out means the word for left goes outside

parts.note: left as in departed, fled
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative who has been excluded showed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' looks like 'excluded', but FLED goes outside AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt is to display ostentatiously, so flaunted means showed off.

clue.text: Cook's utensil encourages vermin

parts.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them
lice are parasitic vermin

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool attracts pests.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg slice is a flat slotted spatula for lifting fried eggs.

clue.text: Calm place might erupt

indicators.note: to erupt is to burst out violently, so the letters of place might are scattered

explanation.surface: A tranquil spot could suddenly explode, like a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegmatic describes someone unexcitable and composed, an even temperament.

clue.text: Annoy a number of patients, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: read number as something that numbs: a hypodermic injection deadens pain for patients

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to irritate and the hypodermic used to numb people.

clue.text: Finish off officer classes

indicators.note: finish off means the end is taken off

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: Terminate the senior officer ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera, plural of genus, are classes in biological taxonomy.

clue.text: God in love with singular goddess

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow

explanation.surface: A deity is smitten with a unique goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian god of the underworld.

clue.text: Where golf pro may be providing lessons?

definitions.meaning: a golf professional is found out on the links where the game is played
a set series of classes, such as one of driving lessons

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a golf links and a planned series of classes.

clue.text: Lack of employment gives one endless recreation

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: read as re-creation, making again, so the letters of endless are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Being out of work means one's leisure time never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreation' poses as leisure but is read as re-creation, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is the state of being without work or occupation.

clue.text: Keep putting odd members of team in control

indicators.note: these letters go inside the word for control

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in keeping a tight rein

indicators.note: the first and third letters of team, its odd-numbered positions

explanation.surface: A manager holds on by putting the oddballs of the squad in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd members of' takes T and A from team.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to keep hold of it.

clue.text: Artist who can't visualise seascapes?

parts.note: split the painter's name into two words: someone who can only envisage dry ground, not the sea

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter, best known for animal pictures and the Trafalgar Square lions.

clue.text: See 11
Weapons from revolutionary times, externally unchanged

indicators.note: externally means the phrase for unchanged sits on the outside

parts.note: as is means left in its present state

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for times is read backwards

parts.note: ages are long times, eras

explanation.surface: Arms dating from an age of revolution have survived untouched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests a political uprising, but it only means turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Assegais are slender spears used by peoples of southern Africa.
